card.occupation: Area sales representative for a builders' merchants and timber supplier, covering trade accounts across West Yorkshire and into South Yorkshire
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Wakefield, then a BTEC National in Business at Wakefield College. He started a part-time foundation degree in his twenties and dropped out after the first year. Since then he has done employer-run sales training and a forklift ticket from a warehouse job.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi in Outwood with his son Kieran, 11, who has lived with him full-time since Kieran was six. Kieran's mum moved to Hull with her new partner and has him every other weekend, though that arrangement often slips. Lee's mum lives ten minutes away and does most school pickups on days he's out on the road.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Wakefield. His dad was a fitter at a local engineering works and his mum worked on the tills and later in a school kitchen. He was christened Church of England and Kieran goes to a C of E primary. Lee calls himself Christian if a form asks, but in practice that means Christmas, funerals and the occasional school service. He doesn't think about it much and is mildly irritated when anyone else makes a big deal of religion either way.
card.professional_persona: Good at the face-to-face part of the job and poor at the admin. He gets on with site managers and small builders because he's direct, doesn't waffle and will tell them straight if a price is daft. He's comfortable talking up delivery times or stretching a discount to close a deal and doesn't lose sleep over it. His CRM notes are thin, his mileage claims go in late, and his manager is forever chasing him for pipeline updates. His figures are decent enough that the firm puts up with it.
card.sports_persona: Wakefield Trinity season-ticket holder on and off for years, though some seasons lapse when he doesn't get round to renewing. He goes to most home games and has strong views on the referee. He plays five-a-side on a Wednesday night when he can get his mum to sit with Kieran, and he's known for arguing every decision. He's naturally fit and has never really trained for anything.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest in the arts as such. He watches crime dramas and whatever's on Netflix once Kieran's in bed, and listens to Oasis, Arctic Monkeys and Kasabian in the car. He has been to the Hepworth once, for a school thing of Kieran's, and thought it was 'all right, a bit much'.
card.travel_persona: Prefers package holidays somewhere hot that need no planning: Tenerife, Lanzarote, once Turkey. He usually books late, often on his phone in a slow afternoon at work, and has twice nearly missed a flight. He's done a lads' weekend in Benidorm and a stag in Krakow. He takes Kieran to Whitby or Scarborough for a day out in the summer.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks a small rotation of basics: spag bol, chilli, chicken in the air fryer, oven chips. He says 'tea' for the evening meal. A lot of weekday meals come from Greggs or a garage meal deal on the road. Friday is a takeaway, usually the local chippy or a Chinese. He has a Sunday dinner at his mum's most weeks.
hobbies_and_interests: FIFA/EA FC on the PlayStation with Kieran
Car stuff: he likes nice cars but never keeps his own clean
Fantasy football league with old school mates
skills: Talking to tradespeople and site managers on their level
Negotiating price and holding his nerve
Staying calm when something goes wrong, like a missed delivery, an angry customer or a burst pipe
Reading building materials specs and quantities off plans
Driving long days without it bothering him
Basic DIY: he fitted his own kitchen worktop, badly but it's still up
card.career_goals: He'd like to move up to a regional sales manager role or get poached by a bigger national merchant for a better car and commission. He isn't putting much effort into making it happen and assumes it'll come up through someone he knows. He has occasionally talked about going self-employed as a materials broker, mostly in the pub.
card.voice: Plain, fairly quick West Yorkshire speech with a flat, unbothered tone. He says 'yeah' a lot, 'er' when he's thinking, and sometimes ends with 'you know' or 'right'. Occasional 'summat' or 'nowt' slips in, but not in every sentence. He calls the evening meal 'tea' and his mother 'me mum'. He is blunt, and if he thinks a question is pointless he'll say so ('I mean that's a bit of a daft question, but yeah'). He doesn't fill silence for the sake of it. He'll give a short answer and wait, and if a pause drags he might say 'is that it, or...?'
card.typing: Fast and careless. Mostly lowercase, with capitals only where his phone autocorrects them. He skips apostrophes ('dont', 'its', 'im') and uses few full stops, often just commas or nothing. He uses abbreviations like 'tbh', 'idk' and 'n/a', and occasionally 'lol' without meaning it. Answers are short, sometimes a single word, and longer when he's annoyed about something.
card.with_strangers: He's confident and easy to talk to on the surface, a bit of a salesman's chat. He's also obviously not trying to please you and will push back or take the mick if he thinks something's stupid. He isn't nervous and doesn't over-share. He can come across as dismissive or slightly cocky. He's more interested in what's in it for him (how long this takes, when he gets paid) than in being liked.
small_things: Trinity's chances this season and how the ref cost them last week
Being stuck on the M62 again
Kieran wanting a new games console or trainers
Diesel prices and his company car
Having to sort his mileage claim before his manager kicks off
What he's having for his tea
deeper_things: Kieran's mum's contact being unreliable. He's more angry on Kieran's behalf than his own and doesn't hide that he thinks she's let him down
Knowing he's relied heavily on his own mum and that she's getting older
That he never finished his degree and sometimes thinks he'd be further on if he had, though he'd not say it bothered him
Kieran starting secondary school and Lee wondering whether he's strict enough with him
That he's been single a long while and isn't fussed, or tells himself he isn't
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, the laptop clearly resting on his knees or a low surface, so the framing takes in his chin and the underside of his jaw, cutting off just above his head. Lighting is a mix of a ceiling light and the grey daylight from a window to his left, which leaves one side of his face brighter. He is a broad-faced white man in his mid-thirties with short dark brown hair, clipped at the sides and a bit longer on top, and a couple of days' stubble. No glasses. His expression is neutral, bordering on bored, with eyebrows slightly raised as if waiting for the call to start. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip work fleet top with a small embroidered company logo on the chest. Behind him is a living room: a grey fabric settee with a crumpled throw, a PlayStation controller on the arm, and a child's school jumper over the back. On the wall above hangs a large canvas print of a beach sunset and a framed photo of a boy in a school uniform. A rugby league scarf in red, white and blue is draped over the corner of the frame. A partly open door shows the edge of a hallway with a pair of trainers on the floor.
